principles: Stop conclusions when evidence is insufficient; a shorter static prompt is not proof of finding recall.
Experiment facts and production lifecycle facts must remain physically and semantically isolated.
Reuse canonical measurement, envelope, and usage-availability semantics to avoid a parallel protocol.
Keep both arms identical for the same pinned input except for prompt shape, and make both replayable by digest.
drivers: Story 3 requires read-only historical material, reproducible measurement, an independent ledger, and explicit INCONCLUSIVE results.
The production agent_prompt handler writes envelope metadata and is unsuitable for historical replay.
Existing pure core assemblers and measurement primitives are sufficient for offline assembly.
Existing historical experiments lack an adjudicated three-class finding corpus, so pinned samples must be added.

options.name: A: experiment-only harness reusing pure core primitives
pros: Exposes no new production write entrypoint
Proves isolation and determinism with minimal changes
cons: Requires a pinned new corpus and adjudication set
Real provider usage remains unavailable until dispatch evidence exists

options.name: B: new production lattice replay CLI and handler
pros: Could later expand to live dispatch
cons: Expands the production command, policy, and process-fact surface
Risks experiment records being mistaken for gate evidence
Adds complexity that this Story does not need

options.name: C: replay historical Stories through the Story-aware agent_prompt handler
cons: Depends on owner, phase, and current HEAD, breaking pinned same-input replay
Violates read-only experiment and production-evidence isolation

chosen: A: experiment-only harness reusing pure core primitives
rationale: Option A directly delivers executable, reproducible, auditable, fail-closed user value. It reuses validated pure assembly and measurement algorithms while limiting every output to experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay. Option B adds unnecessary production process facts and maintenance surface, while option C violates the read-only isolation constraint.

preMortem.scenario: The corpus appears historical but lacks a complete arm or adjudicated finding set.
preMortem.trigger: A sample manifest omits a pinned digest, one of the three class labels, seeded critical/high truth, or either arm.
preMortem.consequence: The harness reports a false finding-recall result.
preMortem.mitigation: Mechanically validate corpus completeness before execution; any missing field makes the whole affected conclusion INCONCLUSIVE and prevents a success claim.

preMortem.scenario: An experiment run contaminates production Story evidence.
preMortem.trigger: The harness calls agent_prompt or Story finding, review, or pass write handlers, or writes Story metadata.
preMortem.mitigation: Import only pure core functions, constrain outputs to the experiment directory, and require production evidence hashes and counts to remain byte-identical before and after selfcheck.

preMortem.scenario: Estimated tokens are presented as provider-processed usage.
preMortem.trigger: The report combines availability layers or replaces unavailable values with zero.
preMortem.consequence: Budget conclusions become false and drive an invalid migration decision.
preMortem.mitigation: Report assembled, known-dispatch, provider, and cache layers separately; retain unavailable plus a reason and never substitute across layers.

preMortem.scenario: The A and B arms receive different inputs beyond prompt shape.
preMortem.trigger: Task context, runtime, model, contract, or execution-environment digests differ.
preMortem.consequence: Finding differences cannot be attributed to prompt modularization.
preMortem.mitigation: Pin shared input and the sole allowed difference in the manifest, then enforce same-input parity before execution.

preMortem.scenario: Repeated runs produce different digests because of timestamps or ordering.
preMortem.trigger: createdAt, JSON key order, finding order, or ledger identity is not canonicalized.
preMortem.consequence: Users cannot reproduce or audit the result.
preMortem.mitigation: Use a pinned timestamp, canonical JSON, stable sorting, identity-keyed records, and a selfcheck that compares core digests across two runs.
